title: French Consulate
capsule: The French Consulate (1799–1804) was the executive government established after Napoleon Bonaparte's coup of 18 Brumaire (9 November 1799) overthrew the Directory, replacing it with three consuls of whom Bonaparte, as First Consul, held effective authority. The Constitution of Year VIII concentrated legislative and executive power, enabling Bonaparte to reorganize the French state through the Napoleonic Code (1804), the Concordat of 1801 with Pius VII, and the creation of the prefectural system. The regime ended when the Senate voted to transform the Consulate into the hereditary First Empire, with Napoleon proclaimed Emperor on 18 May 1804.
